dedupe_keys.name: experimental study on transport and retention dynamics of macroplastics in gully pots

description: Khaled, Qusai and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. A 1:1 gully-pot physical model is tested with flows from 0.2 to 2.0 L/s. Coverage includes retention and transport of bottles, caps, cigarette filters and snack wrappers, with and without sediments. The study reports that high discharges reduce trapping efficiency and that accumulated sediments accelerate plastic transport, especially at high flow. The physical drainage experiment supports assessment of how gully infrastructure controls pollutant transfer. A separate downloadable measurement dataset is not established by this publication metadata. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-nc-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations.
